cases.scope: Hosted non-production password login/logout, refresh rotation, caller-bound profile provisioning and A/B RLS, plus actual Windows Credential Manager cross-process startup restore and account switching on a GitHub-hosted Windows runner. cases.reproduce: python3 scripts/test_hosted_workflow.py; python3 scripts/test_hosted_supabase_probe.py; After the workflow reaches the default branch, configure the protected supabase-staging environment and two distinct pre-provisioned non-production users, then manually dispatch hosted-supabase-acceptance.yml with confirm_non_production=true. The API probe verifies A/B ownership, two independent A sessions, refresh rotation, ensure_profile, own/cross-owner reads and updates, anonymous denial, and scope=local logout. The Windows 2022 job then runs fresh processes in order: A password login and clean close, A refresh-token restore/profile after process restart; restore-a checks the exact GoTrue response token is readable from Credential Manager before ensure_profile, A local logout/credential clear, B password login/profile/logout, and exact-target cleanup. Record the exact run/head and redacted result. The Windows sequence additionally runs prepare-revoked-a and restore-revoked-a in separate processes: local logout revokes A's saved token, the next process must fail restore without profile, explicit login must clear before password Auth and persist rotation before profile.

The Windows fixture uses the real Windows Credential Manager MethodChannel, caller-owned Supabase SDK, GoTrue and PostgREST; it uses an empty in-memory review store and does not exercise learner UI or review submission. It proves process-boundary restore only when the protected workflow actually passes; it does not force a cryptographically expired JWT, OS logoff/power-loss, physical multi-device offline sync or the complete learner journey. The workflow is manual-only, requires explicit non-production confirmation and a protected environment, and must run only on the ephemeral GitHub-hosted windows-2022 runner because cleanup clears that runner user's exact project credential target. Keep pending until the hosted run is observed. An offline regression also forces a refresh response whose returned identity changes after the old refresh token is consumed; the returned session is registered for local cleanup before the identity guard fails, so no rotated session is orphaned. The new server-revoked refresh recovery remains pending until the protected manual hosted workflow passes; it is not a cryptographically expired-token or expiry-window test.
